problems.title: Two positive exponential inputs
problems.question: Find a so log₂(4^x-a)=x has two solutions.
problems.idea: Set t=2^x>0.
steps: Two distinct positive roots require discriminant 1+4a>0 and product -a>0; their sum is 1.
Thus -1/4<a<0. Each positive t gives exactly one x, and its logarithm argument equals t>0.
problems.note: None of the listed parameter sets is exact. The archive’s earliest available scan is printed Variant II (files 2.PDF,3.PDF,4.PDF); Variant I is absent. These explanations correspond to the already selected first available scan, rather than a verified printed Variant I.

problems.title: Combine most of the logarithms
problems.question: Locate 8log₆2+9log₆3 among the printed intervals.
problems.idea: Pair eight copies of each logarithm.
steps: Thus the expression lies strictly between 8 and 9.

problems.title: An oscillating but shrinking sequence
problems.question: Which description is true of aₙ=(1/n)sin(πn/2)?
problems.idea: Bound the sine by 1 in absolute value.
steps: The terms begin 1,0,-1/3,0,1/5, so the sequence is neither increasing nor decreasing.
It is bounded and converges to 0; its changing nonzero amplitudes prevent periodicity.

problems.title: An exponential is automatically below 27
problems.question: Solve (1/3)^(√(2x+5))<27.
problems.idea: Find the square-root domain first.
steps: Every input in the domain satisfies the inequality.

problems.title: Overlap of two opposite congruent cones
problems.question: Two congruent coaxial cones have each apex at the other base’s centre. What percent of one cone’s volume is their overlap?
problems.idea: Their common solid consists of two half-scale cones.
steps: At the middle plane each cone has radius R/2.
The overlap has two halves, each a cone of radius R/2 and height H/2.

problems.title: A logarithm of a nonpositive square
problems.question: Solve log₃(-x²+4x-4)/√(x-2)<0.
problems.idea: The logarithm argument must be positive.
steps: It is never positive, so the expression has no real domain.

problems.title: An exponential sequence limit
problems.question: Find lim(1+1/n)^(-2n).
problems.idea: Use the standard definition of e.
steps: Raise the positive sequence to power -2.

problems.title: Equal spheres and their overlap depth
problems.question: Two equal spheres intersect in a circle of diameter 6 cm. Along the centre line their overlapping segment is 2 cm long. Find their radius.
problems.idea: Let d be the centre distance and R the radius.
steps: Thus R=5 and d=8, consistent with the described intersection.

problems.title: Distance to the projection of a sphere point
problems.question: A radius-5 sphere touches a plane at A. For a sphere point K, KT is perpendicular to the plane and KT=9. Find OT, where O is the centre.
problems.idea: The centre is 5 above the plane, so K is 4 above its level.
steps: OT has vertical component 5 and horizontal component 3.

problems.title: A sphere tangent along triangle sides
problems.question: A right triangle with legs 8,15 has all sides tangent to a sphere whose centre is distance 2 from its plane. Find the sphere radius.
problems.idea: Its planar incircle has radius 3.

problems.title: Check the absolute-value bars in the scan
problems.question: Find the area of the set printed as |x+y|≤1.
problems.idea: This is a strip rather than a closed diamond.
steps: The boundaries are the two parallel lines y=-x-1 and y=-x+1.
The strip extends indefinitely along them and has infinite area.
If the intended condition were |x|+|y|≤1, its diamond would have diagonals 2,2 and area 2.
problems.answer: As printed: infinite area. Under the likely intended |x|+|y|≤1: area 2.
problems.note: The scan appears to put one pair of absolute-value bars around x+y; the extracted transcription inserts separate bars. Both readings and their different consequences are recorded.

problems.title: Leading powers determine a sum limit
problems.question: Find lim(3+6+…+3n)/√(2n⁴+5n²+2).
problems.idea: Use the arithmetic-sum formula and divide by n².

problems.title: A sphere’s planar circumcircle
problems.question: A,B,C lie on a radius-9 sphere, ∠ABC=30° and AC=3 cm. Find the centre’s distance to their plane.
problems.idea: The triangle circumradius is the radius of the sphere section.

problems.title: Frustum height from a sloping generator
problems.question: A cone frustum has base radii 2,8 cm and its generator makes 60° with the base. Find volume.
problems.idea: The generator’s horizontal projection is the radius difference.

problems.title: Convert litres before solving for radius
problems.question: A cylindrical vessel holds 50 litres; its axial-rectangle diagonal makes 45° with the base. Which listed radius is closest?
problems.idea: The angle gives height equal to diameter.
steps: The closest listed value is 20 cm.

problems.title: A square root of a logarithm
problems.question: Solve √(3-log₂|x|)<2.
problems.idea: The radicand must be nonnegative and less than 4.

problems.title: Rotate the shaded remainder of a triangle
problems.question: A right triangle with legs 3,4 contains a semicircle centred on the longer leg, tangent to the shorter leg and hypotenuse. Rotate the shaded remainder about the longer leg. Find volume.
problems.idea: Subtract the sphere formed by the semicircle from the cone formed by the triangle.
steps: Place the longer leg on the y-axis and the shorter on the x-axis. The hypotenuse is 4x+3y=12.
A centre (0,r) tangent to y=0 has distance r from the hypotenuse, giving (12-3r)/5=r and r=3/2.
Rotating the semicircle makes a sphere of volume (4π/3)(3/2)³=9π/2.

problems.title: Roots straddling 1
problems.question: Find b so x²-(log₂b)x-3=0 has one root below 1 and the other above 1.
problems.idea: An upward quadratic is negative strictly between its roots.

problems.title: A bounded input to a logarithmic rational function
problems.question: Find the range of f(x)=log₂(7/(4^(sinx)-2^(sinx)+2)).
problems.idea: Let t=2^(sinx), so 1/2≤t≤2.
steps: Thus 7 divided by it ranges from 7/4 to 4.
problems.note: None of the printed range choices matches this bounded interval.

problems.title: Rotate a right trapezoid about its height
problems.question: A right trapezoid has bases 2,10 and height 3. Rotate it about the perpendicular leg. Find volume.
problems.idea: The result is a cone frustum.

problems.title: Spherical sector and central-angle convention
problems.question: An ice-cream solid is a spherical sector of radius 6 with full central angle 60°. Find its volume.
problems.idea: The axial half-angle is 30°, giving the spherical-cap height.
steps: This includes the cap and its cone to the sphere centre, as required for a spherical sector.
problems.note: No printed option matches radius 6 and full central angle 60°. If 60° were instead the half-angle, the sector volume would be 72π, also absent from the choices.

problems.title: Only the sign of the fixed exponent matters
problems.question: Solve a^[log₀.₄((√11-3)/0.3)]<1.
problems.idea: Compare the logarithm argument with 1.
formulas: √11>3.3, so (√11-3)/0.3>1; base 0.4<1 gives a negative exponent.
steps: For positive a, a to a negative power is below 1 exactly when a>1.

problems.title: A logarithm turns the sum into 1
problems.question: Solve 2^y5^(-x)=200, log₂(x+y)=0, and find y-x.
problems.idea: The logarithm says x+y=1.

problems.title: Maximum integer count in a sliding open interval
problems.question: What is the greatest number of integer solutions of log₄(log₃(x+m))<0?
problems.idea: Convert the nested-log inequality to an interval.
steps: Thus 1-m<x<3-m, an open interval of length 2.
It contains at most two integers, and a noninteger shift such as m=1/2 gives both 1 and 2.

problems.title: Count positive lattice points column by column
problems.question: Count points with natural coordinates satisfying y≤-x²+6x, y≥|x|.
problems.idea: Use positive integers for natural coordinates.
formulas: For x>0, x≤y≤-x²+6x; a column has -x²+5x+1 points.
problems.note: If 0 is included among natural numbers, (0,0) adds one point, making 26. The listed answer uses positive natural numbers.
